messages:
Aria: Repro: magnet-8b-int8 shows a token flip right after a shard-handshake when total prefills exceed ~65535. Prefill=66000, single-token continuation.

Ben: Which handshake version and where exactly is the flip? Paste a snippet.

Aria: run: ./local_infer --model magnet-8b-int8 --ctx 131072 --prefill tests/long_66k.txt --swap-mode fast
Log:
[12:01:02] prefill done tokens=66000
[12:01:10] handshake applied; applied_tokens=440
[12:01:11] cont token expected=' the' got=' tha'

QA Bot: automated longctx-wrap test triggered (id: lc-1769997777). Artifacts: gs://ci/longctx/lc-1769997777/logs.tgz

Kofi: Applied_tokens=440 is suspicious. Should equal 66000 or a delta. Could be integer truncation; 66000 mod 65536 = 464. 440 vs 464 suggests an off-by-24 in the encoder.

Ben: I checked handshake encoder: it packs token_count into uint16 then subtracts a base shim of 24 for alignment. If token_count > 65535 it wraps. That explains the wrap to 464 then minus 24 -> 440.

Aria: Confirmed: switching swap-mode=legacy avoids the problem. Quick fix: clamp or switch to 32-bit field in the handshake encoding. Opening PR.

Kofi: Add a regression test: generate prefills at [65534,65535,65536,66000,120000] and assert token alignment post-handshake vs fp16 baseline.

Aria: Added test to tests/longcontext/handshake_overflow_test.py and put the minimal repro in the run artifacts. Leaving this P1 for onboarding.
